description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

Capgemini is a global business and technology transformation partner helping organizations accelerate digital and sustainable transformation. The company is seeking a Junior Frontend Developer to build and maintain web and mobile application features, write tested code, resolve bugs, use AI-assisted development tools, and collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams.
Junior UI developer building and testing web and mobile application features

Responsibilities:
• Build and maintain UI features across web (React/Angular/Vue) and/or mobile (iOS/Android/cross-platform) applications under senior guidance
• Write clean, tested code following established component and state-management patterns
• Fix bugs, address QA feedback, and implement small enhancements independently
• Use AI coding assistants (GitHub Copilot, Claude, or similar) to speed up development, test writing, and debugging
• Participate in code reviews - both giving and receiving feedback
• Collaborate with designers, QA, and backend engineers to deliver features end-to-end
• Document components and contribute to team knowledge base • Participate in sprint planning, stand-ups, and estimation

Requirements:
• 0-2 years of professional frontend development experience (internships count)
• Foundational knowledge of at least one modern framework (React, Angular, or Vue)
• Comfortable using AI coding assistants (Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or similar) for day-to-day development tasks
• Basic understanding of REST APIs and version control (Git)
• Strong fundamentals in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript/TypeScript
• Eagerness to learn, take feedback, and grow technically

Preferred:
• Exposure to mobile development concepts (native iOS/Android or cross-platform frameworks) is a plus
• Coursework, bootcamp, or personal projects involving AI/LLM integration
• Familiarity with CI/CD basics and automated testing frameworks
• Exposure to Agile/Scrum development environments
• A portfolio or GitHub profile showcasing personal or academic projects
